definition: The sum of the relative atomic masses of all the atoms in a compound's formula. Found by adding up the Ar values of each atom.
The unit used to measure the amount of a substance. One mole of any substance contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number).
The number of particles in one mole of a substance: 6.02 × 10²³. Named after the Italian scientist Amedeo Avogadro.
The mass of one mole of a substance in grams per mole (g/mol). Numerically equal to the relative formula mass.
In a chemical reaction, the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products. Atoms are not created or destroyed — they are rearranged.
A chemical equation in which the number of atoms of each element is the same on both sides. Reflects the conservation of mass.
The reactant that is completely used up in a reaction, limiting the amount of product that can be formed.
The reactant that is not completely used up in a reaction — some remains when the reaction stops.
A measure of how much product is actually obtained compared to the maximum theoretical amount. Calculated as: (actual yield ÷ theoretical yield) × 100.
The maximum mass of product that could be obtained in a reaction, calculated from the balanced equation.
The mass of product actually obtained in a reaction. Usually less than the theoretical yield due to incomplete reactions, side reactions, or losses during purification.
A measure of how much of the reactants end up in the desired product. Calculated as: (Mr of desired product ÷ sum of Mr of all products) × 100.
The amount of solute dissolved in a given volume of solution. Measured in mol/dm³ or g/dm³.
The substance that is dissolved in a solution.
The liquid in which a solute dissolves to form a solution.
A mixture formed when a solute dissolves in a solvent.
A technique used to find the concentration of an unknown solution by reacting it with a solution of known concentration until the reaction is just complete (the end point).
The point in a titration where the reaction is just complete, shown by a permanent colour change in the indicator.
A substance that changes colour depending on whether a solution is acidic or alkaline. Used in titrations to show the end point.
The calculation used to find the number of moles, mass, or molar mass: moles = mass ÷ molar mass (n = m ÷ Mr).
At room temperature and pressure (RTP), one mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³ (24,000 cm³). Used to calculate volumes of gases in reactions.
Standard conditions used in chemistry: a temperature of 25°C and a pressure of 100 kPa. At RTP, 1 mole of gas = 24 dm³.
